text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
All papers lead with Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad saying the goverment is fully committed to the successful completion of the Bakun hydroelectric dam project.
-- Mahathir said action would be taken against government leaders who lead lifestyles beyond the income they had declared when they were appointed.
-- Executive chairman of Bakun dam main contractor Ekran Bhd, Ting Pek Khiing, said four companies controlled by him will lead the local portion of contracts for the project.
-- Fifty-four financial institutions led by Commerce International Merchant Bankers Bhd have underwritten the 375 million shares in the public share offering of Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd.
-- Students who smoke will be caned and those caught puffing four times in school will be expelled, Education Minister Najib Razak said.
-- The government may appoint an acting chief minister for western Malacca state, while its chief minister Mohd Zin Ghani recuperates after a stroke, said Mahathir.

-- Power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd believes its performance should have been better due to its size and capacity, said company executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali over a TV programme. Tenaga on Monday reported net profit of 511 million ringgit for the half-year to February 28.
